case.case_title: Seetha Weerakoon v. Mahendra, O.I.C. Police Station, Galagedera and Others

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was unlawfully detained without being produced before a Magistrate as required by law and without valid detention orders, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed she was detained for a prolonged period without being produced before a Magistrate within 30 days and without valid detention orders covering the entire detention period.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that detention orders under Emergency Regulations authorized the detention and that delays were due to administrative lapses and instructions from the Counter Subversive Unit.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained from 12 August 1989 to 27 August 1990.
Detention order expired on 12 November 1989; no order covered detention until 8 February 1990.
Petitioner was not produced before a Magistrate within 30 days as required by Regulation 19(1).
Petitioner was produced before Magistrate only on 27 August 1990 and remanded to Fiscal custody.
No valid explanation was given for failure to produce petitioner before Magistrate.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained must be produced before a judge within a prescribed time and cannot be held without a legal order. The court emphasized that this is a fundamental safeguard of liberty and must be strictly complied with.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was not produced before a Magistrate within 30 days of arrest, and there was a period without any valid detention order. The court found these failures to be violations of Article 13(2). The explanation of administrative delay or lack of instructions was rejected as insufficient.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge within the prescribed time is unlawful.
Legal detention orders must cover the entire period of detention.
Strict compliance with Article 13(2) is essential to safeguard liberty.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s detention was unlawful and violative of Article 13(2) due to failure to produce her before a Magistrate and absence of valid detention orders for the entire period.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The detention order was quashed, and compensation was awarded to the petitioner.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s prolonged detention without judicial oversight and valid orders was unlawful, directly leading to the relief granted.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was not produced before a Magistrate as required by Regulation 19(1) of the Emergency Regulations. The court held that this failure violated Article 13(2) and that the detention order was invalid for the period without a valid order.
